audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer called this 'a strongly favorable lane for you' and gave Cassiopeia all seven stages, while the full layer gave Pantheon the first four and rated the matchup TRICKY 7/10. The two halves of the page disagreed about who wins the lane.
audit.why: 50.36% over 550 games is dead even, and the kit explains the shape: Comet Spear pokes 575 for 25 mana, Shield Vault is a 600-range point-and-click dash-stun on 13/12/11/10/9s, and Aegis Assault blocks frontal damage on 22/21/20/19/18s. Cassiopeia's kill range is 700 with no dash. Pantheon owns levels 1-3, it evens at 4-5, and Cassiopeia owns 6 onward once Petrifying Gaze can cancel the channel.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-3 Pantheon, 4-5 Skill, 6 and both item stages Cassiopeia, and the early/mid/late prose rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every one of the seven chart rows disagreed across layers: full read Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Skill, Skill, Skill and content read Cassiopeia seven times.
audit.why: Neither layer was right on its own. The full layer had the early game right and the late game wrong; the content layer had the late game right and the early game wrong.
audit.corrected: Both layers moved to Pantheon, Pantheon, Pantheon, Skill, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia — proposed as matched pairs with every why and whys[] rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two abilities had their roles swapped in the content layer: whys[1] called the stun 'his Comet Spear stun' and whys[4] and wants.you[1] called Aegis Assault a dash. Neither is true.
audit.why: Shield Vault (W) is the dash and the stun; Comet Spear (Q) is the spear thrust or throw; Aegis Assault (E) is a channelled shield that makes him invulnerable to damage from the front. The channel means Petrifying Gaze cancels it outright, which is the single most valuable fact on this page and appeared nowhere. Miasma grounds Shield Vault and the Grand Starfall landing. Mortal Will empowers his next spell, so the wind-up is the tell.
audit.corrected: Roles corrected everywhere they appeared, and the R-cancels-the-channel interaction written into the chart, the spikes and the mid-game text.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', and breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all.
audit.why: The whole matchup is a cooldown-timing problem and the page had no numbers in it.
audit.corrected: Shield Vault 13/12/11/10/9s, Aegis Assault 22/21/20/19/18s, Comet Spear 11s at rank 1 for 25 mana, Grand Starfall 180/165/150s at 5500 range — written into cooldowns, trading, spikes and the do's.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string, both pasted under unrelated titles.

edits.before: Pantheon has to walk through your Noxious Blast and Twin Fang poke just to get into Comet Spear range, and every step he takes closing that gap is a step where you're already ticking poison damage onto him. This is a strongly favorable lane for you — as long as you respect his stun range and don't get caught pushed up alone, you should be out-trading him comfortably by level 5.
edits.after: Pantheon walks at you and there is not much you can do about it: Comet Spear pokes from 575 for 25 mana, Shield Vault dashes 600 and stuns point-blank on 13s, and Aegis Assault blocks everything you throw at his front for the length of a 22-second cooldown. Farm what is safe, hold Miasma for the dash rather than the wave, and understand that levels 1 to 3 are his — your job is to reach 6 even.

edits.before: Level 6 gives him Grand Starfall for a flashy global all-in, but Petrifying Gaze punishes the commitment hard since he has no way to disengage after landing — the instant he dives, you stun and burst him down before his combo finishes. Keep playing the poke game and force him into bad engages; there's no good all-in option for him here.
edits.after: Level 6 is where the lane turns. Grand Starfall is a 5500-range global on 180s, but the ability that matters is Aegis Assault: it is a channel, and Petrifying Gaze cancels it outright, taking his frontal invulnerability with it. From here, trade on the 13-second Shield Vault window, ground the dash when he uses it, and stop giving him free 575-range spears.

edits.before: Rylai's shuts his gap-close down completely since the slow keeps him at poke range permanently, and Void Staff with full poison stacks means anything he manages to land still isn't enough to kill you first. Full-build Cassiopeia wins every stage of this matchup as his front-loaded burst kit has no answer to being kept at range and poisoned down over time.
edits.after: Rylai's keeps him outside 600 between Shield Vaults, and that gap is the whole game — Void Staff with stacked poison finally pushes your damage past his front-loaded burst. The pattern late is fixed: ground the dash, cancel Aegis Assault with Petrifying Gaze so the frontal invulnerability never happens, and out-DPS whatever he opens with.
